title: Talos: UAT-12643, suspected North Korea-aligned group, uses Solana transactions to find C2 servers
summary: Cisco Talos tracks UAT-12643, a financially motivated group assessed with low confidence as North Korea-aligned. It targets crypto holders, gamers and VoIP users with the Go-based Overlord RAT, a public Python stealer and a clipboard hijacker. Overlord reads its C2 addresses from Solana memo transactions. Access comes from weaponised LNK, HTA and MSBuild files.
plain: Researchers describe a hacking group that steals crypto and gaming accounts and hides its control servers addresses inside public blockchain transactions.
exec: Blockchain-based C2 cannot be taken down by blocking domains; targeting is crypto and consumer users.
action: Block and hunt using Talos IOCs (Cisco-Talos/IOCs on GitHub, 2026/11), watch for LNK, HTA and MSBuild launches from downloads, and alert on Discord webhook and gofile.io exfiltration.

key_findings: Overlord RAT (35 commands) gets C2 URLs from Solana memo transactions.
Initial access via LNK, HTA and MSBuild files; exfiltration via Discord webhook and gofile.io.
Attribution to North Korea is low confidence.
recommendations: Use the published IOCs and ClamAV and Snort signatures.

review.note: Compared title, date 18 Nov, low-confidence North Korea attribution (Talos's own), 35-command Go RAT, Solana memo C2, LNK/HTA/MSBuild access, Discord/gofile exfil and GitHub IOCs against the Talos post; actor flag is a false positive as the summary says Talos assesses it
